name: White rose dumpling
summary: White rose is Hoi An’s steamed shrimp-and-pork dumpling, its thin wrapper pinched to look like a rose, topped with fried shallot and dipped in sweet-sour fish sauce. Eat it warm, one dumpling to a bite.
origin: Hoi An. Hoa families in the port shaped it from a Chinese há cảo, so the white bánh bao looks like a rose. The English name is said to come from a guest in the early 1990s who could not remember the Vietnamese one. The wrapper is rice flour made with the same well water as cao lầu, though some cooks use a wheat flour filtered until it is clear.
taste: The filling is sweet with shrimp, or shrimp and pork with wood-ear mushroom, under fried shallot and scallion.
The wrapper is thin and translucent, and the dip is sour, hot, salty, and sweet in balance.
howToEat: One dumpling is one bite. Dip it in the sweet-sour fish sauce and eat it warm.
A cold plate misses the wrapper. Take it as a small plate, not the whole lunch.
where: The old streets where it was carried: Lê Lợi, Trần Phú, Nguyễn Thái Học, and Bạch Đằng.
seoDescription: White rose is Hoi An’s steamed dumpling, bánh bao bánh vạc. Eat it warm, one bite, with fish sauce, on Lê Lợi, Trần Phú, Nguyễn Thái Học, or Bạch Đằng.
